# RingaRoofer

> RingaRoofer (ringaroofer.com) is a roofing referral service for U.S. homeowners. Calling (855) 635-9281 connects a homeowner with an independent roofing company that serves their area, for roof repair, leak repair, roof inspections, storm and hail repair, emergency roofing and tarping, roof replacement, new roofs and re-roofs on shingle, metal, flat, tile, slate and cedar shake roofs. It does not do roofing work and does not charge homeowners.

- [Asphalt shingles or a metal roof: which is right for me?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/asphalt-shingles-vs-metal/): Shingles suit almost any home and are the most common choice. Metal lasts much longer, sheds snow and handles wind well. The choice comes down to how long…
- [What's the difference between architectural and three-tab shingles?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/architectural-vs-three-tab-shingles/): Architectural shingles are thicker, layered and more textured, and they handle wind better. Three-tab shingles are flat and single-layer, and many roofers…
- [Is a metal roof noisy in the rain?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/is-a-metal-roof-noisy/): Not usually. Over solid decking and underlayment, a metal roof sounds much like any other roof. The loud rain on metal you may picture is from barns with…
- [What is a standing seam metal roof?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/standing-seam-metal-roof/): Standing seam panels run from ridge to eave with raised seams that lock together and hide the fasteners. With no exposed screws, there are fewer places…
- [What are the options for a flat roof?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/flat-roof-options/): The main choices are TPO (a white single-ply membrane), EPDM (black rubber) and modified bitumen. Each needs good drainage, since water moves slowly on…
- [Why does water pool on my flat roof?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/water-pooling-on-flat-roof/): Clogged drains, sagging decking or a poor slope. Water that sits for more than a couple of days after rain wears out the membrane faster and finds any…
- [Can a tile roof be repaired?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/tile-roof-repair/): Yes. Cracked or slipped tiles can be replaced one at a time. Often the real issue is the underlayment beneath the tiles, which wears out before the tiles…
- [How long does a slate roof last?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/slate-roof-life/): Natural slate can last 75 years or more. The nails and flashing often wear out before the slate itself, so many slate roofs are repaired rather than…
- [How do I keep a cedar shake roof lasting?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/cedar-shake-upkeep/): Keep it clear of leaves and moss, keep branches trimmed back so it dries out, and replace split or curled shakes early.
- [What are impact-resistant shingles?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/impact-resistant-shingles/): Shingles made to resist hail better than standard shingles, often called Class 4. They're popular in hail-prone states like Texas, Colorado and Oklahoma.
- [How often should I have my roof inspected?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/how-often-roof-inspection/): Once a year is a good habit, plus after major storms. Roofs over 15 years old benefit from more regular checks.
- [What does a roof inspection include?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/what-does-roof-inspection-include/): A roofer checks shingles or roofing, flashing, vent boots, ridge caps, the attic for stains and ventilation, and the decking for soft spots. Ask for…
- [Is moss on my roof a problem?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/moss-on-roof/): Yes, over time. Moss holds moisture against the roof and can lift shingle edges. It's most common on shady, damp slopes.
- [Why are there shingle granules in my downspouts?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/roof-granules-in-downspout/): A few granules are normal on a new roof. A lot of them on an older roof means the shingles are wearing out, or hail knocked them loose.
- [Why does attic ventilation matter for my roof?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/attic-ventilation-and-roof/): Good ventilation keeps the attic cooler in summer and drier in winter. Poor ventilation cooks shingles from below, causes ice dams and leads to moisture…
- [I can see daylight in my attic. Is that bad?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/daylight-in-attic/): Daylight through the roof boards means there's an opening where water can get in too. Light at ridge or eave vents can be normal; light through the roof…
- [Do branches touching the roof cause problems?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/branches-touching-roof/): Yes. Branches scrape off granules, drop debris that holds moisture, and can break shingles or fall in storms. Keep them several feet away from the roof.
- [What should I check on my roof before winter?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/roof-checklist-before-winter/): Look for missing or lifted shingles, loose flashing, worn vent boots and clogged valleys, and make sure the attic is well insulated and ventilated to…
- [How do I find a good roofer near me?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/how-to-find-a-roofer-near-me/): Ask how long they've worked in your area, ask for local references, confirm the credentials your state requires, and get the scope of work in writing. Or…
- [What questions should I ask a roofer?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/questions-to-ask-a-roofer/): Ask how long they've worked locally, who will be on the roof, what the written scope includes, how they protect your property, how they handle surprises…
- [How fast can a roofer come out?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/how-fast-can-a-roofer-come/): Often within a few days, and the same or next day for active leaks or open roofs. After big storms roofers book up quickly, so call early.
- [Do roofers work in winter?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/do-roofers-work-in-winter/): Yes. Roofers repair leaks and handle emergencies year-round, and many replace roofs in winter when the weather allows.
- [A roofer says my whole roof needs replacing. How do I know?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/roofer-says-whole-roof-needs-replacing/): Ask for photos of the problems on each slope and an explanation of why a repair won't hold. It's reasonable to get a second roofer's opinion before a big…
- [I just bought a house. Should I get the roof checked?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/roofing-after-buying-a-house/): Yes. A roof inspection gives you a baseline: how old it is, what needs attention soon and what can wait. It's much easier to plan than to react to a leak.
- [What should be written down before a roofing job starts?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/what-is-included-in-roof-job/): The scope of work: materials and color, what gets torn off, how decking repairs are handled, flashing and vents, start and finish timing, cleanup, and who…
- [Someone knocked on my door offering a new roof. What should I do?](https://ringaroofer.com/questions/roofer-door-to-door/): Don't sign anything on the doorstep. Ask for a local address, references and the credentials your state requires, and take time to get a second opinion.
